name: The Anchor in 3D
body: Ability 3. Dean chose a set swing arc between two anchor points. A `swing_arc` world entity marks the start post; its `end` property is the far post. Jumping beside the start post swings the player along a fixed pendulum arc to the far post, with no steering and no way to fall. Cooperative form: the first arc only works while the companion stands by the start post (`needs_companion`). Solo form: the second arc, beyond her last stop, always works.

comments.text: Filed 2026-11-16 before any code, from Dean's request to start using the Crimson and Thorn mechanics.
Dean answered q1 on 2026-11-16: set swing arc. Card updated before any code; slice 3 builds it.
Built in slice 3 as a set swing arc: see docs/crimson-and-thorn-slice.md ('Slice 3') and the test engine/tests/host/the-anchor-swings-across-the-gap.

plan: 1. `Anchor` entity, `AnchorSystem` (start test, arc maths, advance). 2. `Player.SwingTo`, Simulate runs the swing instead of Move. 3. Streets extended past the far block: two 12 m chasms, one arc each, a checkpoint and gem on each landing. 4. Tests, autopilot, docs, decision. Also the three slice 2 review nits.
acceptance_criteria: The first arc works only with the companion beside the post; the second works alone
A swing can't be fallen out of and ends on the far ledge
A headless keyboard test swings both arcs

questions.text: Which form should the Anchor take in 3D: a set swing arc between two anchor points, a physics rope, or a grapple that pulls the player to the point?
questions.recommendation: A: a set swing arc between two anchor points. It is deterministic, easy to author in the editor and easy to read in a tutorial; a physics rope can come later.
questions.answer: A: a set swing arc between two anchor points (Dean, 2026-11-16).
